source:
Create a AAA-quality endless runner for Roblox inspired by the fast-paced gameplay of classic endless runners like Temple Run 2. The experience should capture the same adrenaline, fluid movement, exploration, and progression while using entirely original characters, environments, animations, music, sounds, UI, and level assets.
The game should feel polished enough to compete with top Roblox experiences.
Core Gameplay
Create an endless runner where the player automatically runs forward.
The player can:
 • Swipe Left → Turn Left
 • Swipe Right → Turn Right
 • Swipe Up → Jump
 • Swipe Down → Slide
 • Collect coins
 • Dodge obstacles
 • Navigate branching paths
 • Achieve high scores
 • Complete missions
 • Unlock cosmetics and characters
Movement should be smooth and highly responsive.

Motion Controls
On supported mobile devices, add optional motion controls using the device's accelerometer and gyroscope.
Features:
 • Tilt left/right to steer or subtly change lane position
 • Optional head-look camera effect
 • Motion sensitivity slider
 • Calibration screen
 • Toggle motion controls on/off
 • Automatic fallback to swipe controls if motion sensors are unavailable
 • Low-latency filtering to reduce jitter
 • Dead zones and smoothing for comfortable play
Motion controls should enhance gameplay without replacing core swipe controls.

Endless World Generation
Implement procedural generation that creates an endless path while maintaining handcrafted quality.
Include diverse original environments such as:
 • Ancient jungle ruins
 • Mountain temples
 • Lava caverns
 • Ice canyons
 • Desert ruins
 • Floating islands
 • Bamboo forests
 • Waterfalls
 • Forgotten cities
 • Underground caverns
Generation should avoid impossible obstacle combinations and maintain fair difficulty.

Obstacles
Create a large variety of original obstacles:
 • Gaps
 • Broken bridges
 • Fallen trees
 • Rolling boulders
 • Rotating blades
 • Swinging axes
 • Spike traps
 • Crumbling floors
 • Fire traps
 • Moving platforms
 • Collapsing bridges
 • Narrow ledges
 • Climbing sections
 • Rope swings
 • Zip lines
Difficulty should scale naturally as the run progresses.

Collectibles
Implement:
 • Coins
 • Rare gems
 • Power crystals
 • Treasure chests
 • Mystery relics
 • Keys
 • Daily collectibles
 • Seasonal collectibles

Power-ups
Create an extensible power-up system including:
 • Coin magnet
 • Temporary shield
 • Speed burst
 • Double coins
 • Slow-motion
 • Invincibility
 • Extra life
 • Auto-collect
 • Lucky treasure boost
Each should include:
 • Visual effects
 • Audio feedback
 • UI timers
 • Upgrade paths

Enemy Chase
Create an original pursuing creature that keeps pressure on the player.
Features:
 • Dynamic catch-up system
 • Difficulty scaling
 • Different chase phases
 • Escape mechanics
 • Cinematic introductions
 • Intelligent obstacle interaction

Missions
Implement hundreds of procedurally generated missions such as:
 • Collect coins
 • Travel distance
 • Jump count
 • Slide count
 • Near misses
 • Perfect turns
 • Consecutive runs
 • Power-up usage
 • Treasure collection

Progression
Create long-term progression:
 • Character unlocks
 • Outfit customization
 • Cosmetic trails
 • Pets
 • Skill upgrades
 • Permanent upgrades
 • Daily rewards
 • Weekly events
 • Achievements
 • Prestige system

Graphics
Create high-quality original visuals featuring:
 • Dynamic lighting
 • Volumetric fog
 • Weather
 • Water effects
 • Particle systems
 • Animated foliage
 • Day/night cycle
 • Cinematic camera
 • Smooth animations
 • Optimized performance across devices

Audio
Compose completely original music inspired by adventurous orchestral and tribal themes.
Include:
 • Ambient exploration music
 • Chase music
 • Menu music
 • Victory sounds
 • Coin collection
 • Power-ups
 • Environmental ambience
Do not use copyrighted music.

Roblox Features
Integrate:
 • DataStore
 • ProfileService
 • Leaderboards
 • Badges
 • Daily rewards
 • Cloud saves
 • Cross-device support
 • Mobile optimization
 • Console support
 • PC support

Performance
Optimize for:
 • 60+ FPS on modern devices
 • Graceful quality scaling
 • Streaming Enabled compatibility
 • Efficient procedural generation
 • Object pooling
 • Minimal memory usage

Code Architecture
Use clean, modular Luau code with separate systems for:
 • Runner Controller
 • Input Manager
 • Motion Control Manager
 • Procedural Generation
 • Obstacle Manager
 • Collectible Manager
 • Mission System
 • Progression System
 • Save Manager
 • UI Framework
 • Audio Manager
 • Camera Controller

QA & Polish
Do not stop after the first playable version.
Continue iterating by:
 • Automatically testing every gameplay mechanic
 • Verifying procedural generation never creates impossible paths
 • Stress-testing long runs
 • Testing all motion controls across supported devices
 • Optimizing performance
 • Eliminating bugs
 • Refining animations, controls, camera, and game feel
Repeat testing and refinement until the experience is polished, performant, and feels like a premium endless runner with original content suitable for Roblox.

answers.ask: How long should one generated stretch be before the biome changes?
answers.answer: Use short, readable biome stretches of roughly 60–90 seconds of running before transitioning to the next environment, with a brief blended transition segment.

answers.ask: How often should the path fork, and do the forks rejoin or commit the player to a branch?
answers.answer: Present a fork about every 20–30 seconds on average, and have branches rejoin after a short alternate segment so runs remain procedurally manageable and fair.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: How long should one generated stretch be before the biome changes? A: Use short, readable biome stretches of roughly 60–90 seconds of running before transitioning to the next environment, with a brief blended transition segment.
- [author] free — Q: How often should the path fork, and do the forks rejoin or commit the player to a branch? A: Present a fork about every 20–30 seconds on average, and have branches rejoin after a short alternate segment so runs remain procedurally manageable and fair.
- [agent_inferred] cleanup placement — Q: How far behind the camera should cleared geometry be recycled? A: Place the cleanup volume two full modular chunks behind the active camera.

## Enriched image prompt
Build an original polished endless adventure-runner world as a continuously generated, free-steering path. Use modular chunks with perfectly matching entry and exit pivots, speed-scaled obstacle spacing, and a horizon hidden by fog, bends, or terrain. Change biomes every 60–90 seconds through short blended transitions among ancient jungle ruins, mountain temples, lava caverns, ice canyons, desert ruins, floating islands, bamboo forests, waterfalls, forgotten cities, and underground caverns. Add a fork roughly every 20–30 seconds; each branch is a short fair alternate route that rejoins the main path.

Distribute gaps, broken bridges, fallen trees, rolling boulders, rotating blades, swinging axes, spike traps, crumbling floors, fire traps, moving platforms, collapsing bridges, narrow ledges, climbing sections, rope swings, and zip lines without impossible combinations. Lay out readable trails for coins, rare gems, power crystals, treasure chests, mystery relics, keys, daily collectibles, and seasonal collectibles. Reserve placements for coin magnets, temporary shields, speed bursts, double coins, slow-motion, invincibility, extra lives, auto-collect, and lucky treasure boosts. Keep one original pursuing-creature origin behind the runner and preserve entirely original characters, environments, and assets.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Infinite Runner because forward movement is automatic through an endless generated path.

## Shape and preset
Use `lane-free`: tilt and swipe input steer continuously across the corridor rather than snapping among fixed lanes. The matched preset is Free Runner, extended with chase pressure, moving hazards, branching chunks, and many biome sets.

## Config requirements
Use `chunk-modular` for deterministic chunks with matching pivots and fair branch-and-rejoin variants. Use `obstacle-jump`, `obstacle-moving`, and `hazard-kill` for all stated static, moving, and run-ending obstacles. Use `barrier-horizon` to hide the live chunk frontier. Use universal `terrain-relief` for mountain, canyon, and ruin stretches without overhang. Use `reveal-exit`, taken from Adventure's catalogue row, for blended outdoor-to-cavern transitions. Use `marker-distance` for subtle environmental progress increments.

## Layout requirements
Place `collectible-nodes` Collectibles for all seven stated collectible families along safe and risky lines. Place `powerup-buffs` PowerUps for all nine stated boost families. Place one `spawner-npc` Spawner, taken from Survival's catalogue row, behind the runner for the original pursuing creature. Place one `trigger-despawn` TriggerZone two full modular chunks behind the camera. Input, scoring, missions, progression, UI, audio, saves, and device controls are mechanics.

## Layout components
The build is an endless queue of compatible path chunks, including straight, turn, fork, rejoin, obstacle, and blended-biome transition pieces. Each 60–90-second biome stretch draws from one of the ten named environments. Branches appear about every 20–30 seconds and always rejoin after a short alternate segment. The corridor boundary is formed by each biome's terrain, ruins, cliff edges, or cavern walls, with the active horizon occluded.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: the endless chunk pivots, speed-legal obstacle sequence, forks, and rejoins must be valid before each biome is dressed. `authored_plan` is unavailable because this is neither a supported maze nor a racing route.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is medium per active chunk, while endless extent is created by streaming the queue; individual obstacles and pickups must remain legible at speed. The theme is original cinematic adventure spanning ten natural and ruin biomes. The pipeline requires `P6` for structurally valid endless generation, `tiered` for mountain and canyon relief, and `P3` for transitions between outdoor stretches and underground cavern interiors.

options.text: Deterministic modular runner chunks with perfectly matching entry and exit pivots, including straight, turn, fork, rejoin, obstacle, and blended-biome transition pieces.
Jump obstacles and gaps such as gaps, broken bridges, narrow ledges, rope swings, and zip lines, spaced to remain clearable at speed.
Moving hazards such as rolling boulders, rotating blades, swinging axes, moving platforms, and collapsing bridges, with speed-scaled fair timing.
Run-ending hazards including spike traps, crumbling floors, fire traps, and chase pressure that ends the run on contact.
Occlude the live chunk frontier using horizon fog, bends, or terrain so the spawning boundary is hidden.
Terrain relief for mountain, canyon, and ruin stretches without overhang, including cliffs, ridges, and readable elevation changes.
Subtle environmental progress increments that communicate distance and pace along the run.
Readable pickup trails and reserved placements for collectibles: coins, rare gems, power crystals, treasure chests, mystery relics, keys, daily collectibles, and seasonal collectibles.
Reserved placements for boosts: coin magnets, temporary shields, speed bursts, double coins, slow-motion, invincibility, extra lives, auto-collect, and lucky treasure boosts.
One original pursuing-creature origin behind the runner.
A cleanup trigger volume that recycles cleared geometry two full modular chunks behind the active camera.

layout.composition: An endless free-steering corridor presented as a streaming queue of modular chunks: the active runnable path in the foreground/midground, with the next chunk frontier hidden by fog, bends, or terrain; biome dressing changes across short blended transition segments.

zones.name: Active corridor chunk queue
zones.role: Continuously generated free-steering runner corridor made of straight, turn, fork, rejoin, obstacle, and blended-biome transition chunks; maintains valid fork-and-rejoin topology and speed-legal obstacle spacing.
zones.where: extends forward from the runner/camera through the horizon-occluded frontier
zones.size: medium per active chunk; endless via streaming

zones.name: Biome stretch
zones.role: A 60–90 second readable stretch themed to one of ten environments, followed by a brief blended transition into the next.
zones.where: along the forward run direction, cycling over time
zones.size: 60–90 seconds of running per biome stretch

zones.name: Fork and rejoin segment
zones.role: Short fair alternate branch that splits from the main corridor and rejoins after a short segment to keep runs manageable and fair.
zones.where: appears along the forward path at intervals
zones.size: fork about every 20–30 seconds on average; short branch length

layout.terrain: Biome-specific terrain and ruins forming the corridor boundary (terrain, ruins, cliff edges, or cavern walls), with mountain/canyon relief and blended outdoor-to-cavern transitions; horizon occluded by fog, bends, or terrain.
layout.boundary: Corridor boundaries defined by each biome's terrain/ruins/cliff edges/cavern walls; the active horizon/frontier is occluded.
layout.theme: Original cinematic adventure spanning ten natural and ruin biomes (ancient jungle ruins, mountain temples, lava caverns, ice canyons, desert ruins, floating islands, bamboo forests, waterfalls, forgotten cities, underground caverns).

render.why: The endless chunk pivots, speed-legal obstacle sequence, forks, and rejoins must be valid before each biome is dressed.
